description: We need to build a game where the player is an astronaut and their own doctor on a 12-month trip to Mars. Each month they get 2 body scans and 3 care hours, and they must keep five body systems healthy while space wears them down.
summary: Cosmic Clinic is a health monitoring software designed for astronauts to manage their health during space missions. It tracks 11 health metrics, including heart rate, blood oxygen, and radiation exposure, using an alert system to advise astronauts on necessary actions. The software has evolved from its initial version, Space Health Buddy, to include features like live health charts and a mission control dashboard. It provides real-time alerts for emergencies, such as radiation spikes and CO₂ scrubbing issues, ensuring crew safety in challenging conditions. A demonstration showed its functionality over 72 mission hours.
details:
Cosmic Clinic is a Python-based health monitoring application designed to help astronauts maintain their health and safety during space missions. It acts as a virtual flight doctor by monitoring 11 different health readings, including heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, energy, hydration, stress, sleep debt, radiation exposure, bone density, and muscle mass.

The software continuously tracks each crew member's health and calculates an overall health score. It uses colour-coded indicators (green, yellow, and red) to identify safe, warning, and dangerous conditions. When a health reading becomes concerning, the application displays alerts and provides recommendations to help astronauts decide what action to take.

Cosmic Clinic also simulates realistic space emergencies, including solar flares, CO₂ scrubber faults, long night shifts, and micrometeoroid alarms. Astronauts can respond using actions such as eating, drinking, exercising, resting, sleeping, performing medical scans, and entering a radiation shelter.

The project was developed using Python and the Tkinter library. It includes interactive dashboards, live heart-rate charts, keyboard shortcuts, a mission log, and a health monitoring system. The software runs locally on a computer without requiring additional downloads.

Our project is creative because it combines astronaut health monitoring with an interactive space mission simulation. Instead of simply displaying health information, it allows users to experience how different space conditions affect astronauts and how their decisions influence crew health.

The intended impact is to demonstrate how technology can support astronaut health, improve awareness of space-related medical risks, and help prepare for safer long-duration space missions. Future improvements could include smartwatch sensor integration, AI-powered health predictions, personalized astronaut health plans, and communication with mission control on Earth.
